data.claim: build_parser() attaches a resolvable completion kind to every argument action: choices -> enum, an id-like name or an id positional of a record verb -> id:<kind>, a path name/metavar -> path/dir, else none. An argument that is id-like or has a closed value set yet resolves to none fails a ratchet test unless explicitly exempt.
data.falsifier: A probe over build_parser() shows a choices-bearing or id-named action that resolves to none with no exemption, or an action whose kind changes without any code change.
data.mechanism: kinds.infer() is a pure stdlib function on (dest, choices, metavar, positional, record_kind). Param.complete declares, add_to attaches the resolved kind onto the argparse action, hand-written add_argument calls use a one-line helper. completion_exemptions.py lists any argument that must not complete, with a reason.
data.probe: python3 -c: walk build_parser(), count actions; enumerate options/positionals with choices and their dests/metavars; count id-like dests (item/phase/bug/lesson/.../id) and path/dir metavars.
data.probe_output: options 2109, positionals 136, subparsers 28; 19 options with choices (--kind, --outcome, --status, --result, --sort, --mode, --bump, --launch, --cwd, --reviewer, --applies-to, --into, --format, --at, ...); 11 positionals with choices; metavars ID x37, DIR x3, NAME x2. A deterministic name->kind table covers every entry; none requires per-argument code.
data.question: Can every ddflow argument's shell-completion value kind be declared on the argument (Param.complete) and inferred from its own name/choices/type, so a new command, option, choice or record kind needs no per-argument completion code, and a forgotten declaration is caught by a ratchet instead of silently offering nothing?

evidence.note: R-completion-declare-kind CONFIRMED: probe over build_parser() shows 2109 options/136 positionals/28 subparsers; 19 options and 11 positionals carry choices (--kind/--outcome/--status/--result/--sort/--mode/...), metavars ID x37/DIR x3; the name->kind inference table (choices->enum, id-like name->id:<kind>, path/dir metavar->path/dir) decides every argument deterministically from its own action, no per-argument code. Falsifier (a choices/id-like action resolving to none without exemption) is exactly what the ratchet asserts against.

chunk_findings.detail: `metavar="PATH"` is classified as a directory. `DIR_METAVARS` is `{"DIR", "PATH"}` and that branch returns `"dir"` before `FILE` is considered, and nothing maps `PATH` to `"path"`. Given `infer("spec", metavar="PATH")` the result is `"dir"`, so TAB only offers directories and a file-valued `--spec PATH` cannot be completed. The kind vocabulary treats `"path"` as file paths and the infer docstring claims `DIR`/`PATH`/`FILE` resolve to dir/path; this input gets the wrong one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/kinds.py:infer

chunk_findings.detail: Path inference never sees the argument type, despite the change requiring paths to come from the type. `infer` only takes name, choices, metavar, positional, and record kind. Given an action `add_argument("--config", type=pathlib.Path)` (dest `config`, metavar defaulting to `CONFIG`, no choices), `infer("config")` returns `"none"`, so the path is free text and will not complete. Named exceptions in `PATH_NAMES`/`DIR_NAMES` do not cover ordinary typed path parameters.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/kinds.py:infer

chunk_findings.detail: The loop asserts `kind == "enum"` whenever `action.choices is not None`, but `_resolve` returns a declared `complete` before inference. Intent allows `complete` of `phase`, `gate`, `agent`, `state`, `path`, `dir`, or `none` even when choices are set, and "choices -> enum" applies only when complete is unset. Given an action with `choices=("open", "closed")` and `complete="state"`, `_resolve` returns `"state"` and the assertion fails, so a correct future declaration is rejected by CI.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_declare.py:test_inference_resolves_every_choices_and_id_argument

chunk_findings.detail: `kinds.declare_id_kind("widget")` mutates the same registry `_record_kind` reads via `kinds.id_kinds()`, and nothing removes `"widget"` afterward. Run this test, then any later test (or a reordered `test_no_free_text_id_like_argument_is_silently_skipped`) that expects id kinds to match the RecordKind registry: `"widget"` is still registered, so inference and the ratchet see a kind the process did not start with.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_declare.py:test_canary_a_new_id_parameter_completes_with_no_completion_code

chunk_findings.detail: `infer` checks `metavar == "ID"` before the name-kind tables, so a more specific name is discarded. The docstring says a name that spells a record kind or a fixed vocabulary kind wins; `infer("bug", metavar="ID")` returns `"id"` instead of `"id:bug"`, and `infer("agent", metavar="ID")` returns `"id"` instead of `"agent"`. Completion then offers every record id rather than that kind or the agent vocabulary.
